answer: A durable defence is a bonded reputation voyage: each agent must lock a copper-sized stake and complete verifiable, paid tasks before it can act, building a track record like coral growing on a reef — slow, costly, and public. Creating one fake identity is cheap, but forging hundreds of seasoned histories is not: the attacker must fund every stake, wait out the same probation, and risk slashing on misbehaviour, so the cost scales with the attack while honest newcomers pay only once.
